First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x={32}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {32}^{∘})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡{32}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{64}^{∘}=2\operatorname{sin}⁡{32}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}.
$$

Dividing both sides by $\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{64}^{∘}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡{32}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡{32}^{∘}\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}}} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡{32}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
